title: Case: Policy officer's message about his toner parcel
context: A toner parcel from Tallowmere Goods was sent to Greer Dunmore at the Office of the Port Commissioner, Corvel Quarter, and he has been in touch with the desk about it this morning.
initial_request:
[Business portal mobile app: this message was queued while the device was offline and has now been sent. Composed 07 Oct 08:39.]

Hi, where's my toner? DL-6167. Tracking hasn't moved and I need it for room 4.12 this morning.

events.from: Greer Dunmore, policy officer, Office of the Port Commissioner
events.body: Hi, where is DL-6167? Tracking hasn't changed since yesterday and I need the toner for the printer in room 4.12 this morning.
DL-6167 (TG-6891, toner cartridges, Office of the Port Commissioner): the recipient says tracking has not updated since yesterday. Could you confirm its current status?

events.from: IT service desk, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Planned maintenance: the work queue will be read-only on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Messages sent in that window are queued and delivered afterwards.
DL-6167 delivered 7 Oct 07:58 to the Office of the Port Commissioner mailroom, signed 'T. Gallimore, mailroom'. Tracking display was delayed by a scanner sync issue; now updated.

This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Wednesday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.

events.to: Greer Dunmore, policy officer, Office of the Port Commissioner
events.body: Dispatch confirms DL-6167 was delivered to your mailroom at 07:58 today and signed for by T. Gallimore. The tracking page was slow to update and now shows it. The mailroom should be able to tell you where it has been put.
Route plan for depot BR-9 published for Tuesday. 37 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.

events.from: Quillon Gallimore, mailroom, Office of the Port Commissioner
events.body: Confirming DL-6167 was received at 07:58 and logged as MR-2134. Mr Dunmore came down and collected it at 09:58.

events.from: Greer Dunmore, policy officer, Office of the Port Commissioner
events.body:
Got it from the mailroom, thanks very much. Printer's back up.

Label scan attached for reference: label-scan-404.txt

attachments.name: label-scan-404.txt
attachments.text:
LABEL SCAN
Shipment: DL-66511
Consignee: Verity Ashdown
Address: 38 Mill Yard

Scanned: 2028-10-04T08:41:00Z

must: Takes no action and logs why: the message was written at 08:39, before the desk's answer, and only sent late from the offline queue; it duplicates the 08:41 question already answered.
Bases that on the facts in the thread: Dispatch confirmed delivery at 07:58, the mailroom logged it as MR-2134 and saw him collect it at 09:58, and he said at 10:15 that he had it.
must_not: Sends Greer Dunmore another message restating the delivery or asking if he still needs help.
Contacts Dispatch, the mailroom or Tallowmere again about DL-6167.
Opens a trace, investigation or missing-parcel claim for DL-6167.
Treats the queued message as a new report that the parcel is missing.
Treats label-scan-404.txt as evidence about DL-6167: it is the label of a different shipment (DL-66511)
Tells anyone that DL-6167 was delivered or left in a safe place on the strength of label-scan-404.txt
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments

rationale: Rule-made from city-040: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. label-scan-404.txt belongs to another shipment (DL-66511); the key is the seed's plus must_not rules. 5 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
